title: Add KMS envelope encryption support for Private backup artifacts
creator: Ethan Park
content:
## Context
Private customers (VPC + on-prem, incl. air-gapped) are explicitly asking for customer-controlled encryption for backup artifacts. Today the backup prototype produces an encrypted artifact with static/local keying assumptions. We need envelope encryption with pluggable KMS/HSM providers so that:
- Backups are always encrypted at rest
- Key material is not persisted by Redwood tooling
- Enterprises can use their existing KMS (AWS KMS in VPC; HSM-backed KMS or on-prem equivalents)
- Restores remain deterministic and debuggable (manifest captures enough metadata)

This ticket implements the encryption architecture + provider interface and wires it into `backup create` / `restore apply`, plus operator-facing docs updates.

## Goals
1) Implement envelope encryption for backup artifacts in the private installer.
2) Provide a KMS provider interface supporting at least one production provider (AWS KMS) and a “no-KMS”/dev provider for test/dev.
3) Define key rotation expectations and what must be retained to restore older backups.
4) Add operator documentation and runbook updates covering configuration, failure modes, and audit evidence.

## Non-goals
- Building a full KMS management UI in Console.
- Supporting every vendor KMS at GA. We will ship a provider interface + AWS KMS reference implementation and document how to add additional providers.
- Backing up plaintext secrets. Backups must contain *references* to secrets (or rehydration instructions), not secret material.

## Proposed design (high-level)
### Envelope encryption
- Generate a one-time Data Encryption Key (DEK) per backup artifact.
- Encrypt the artifact payload with AES-256-GCM (streaming-friendly) using the DEK.
- Wrap (encrypt) the DEK using KMS (KEK managed by customer).
- Store wrapped DEK + KMS metadata in the backup manifest.

### Manifest fields (minimum)
Manifest must record enough to restore without guessing:
- `encryption.scheme`: `envelope-aes256-gcm`
- `encryption.provider`: e.g. `aws-kms`
- `encryption.kms_key_id`: full ARN or stable key identifier
- `encryption.wrapped_dek`: base64
- `encryption.aad`: additional authenticated data (include cluster ID + backup ID + format version)
- `encryption.created_at`
- `format_version`

### Provider interface
Introduce a provider abstraction in the installer:
- `EncryptDEK(plaintext_dek, context) -> wrapped_dek, key_metadata`
- `DecryptDEK(wrapped_dek, context, key_metadata) -> plaintext_dek`

Where `context` must be deterministic and included in the manifest AAD. Context is used to bind the wrapped key to the intended backup/cluster and prevent cross-artifact substitution.

### Key rotation expectations
- New backups always use the configured KMS key at time of backup.
- Restores of old backups require the ability to decrypt the wrapped DEK (i.e., old key versions must remain usable).
- Document the operator requirement: **do not disable or schedule deletion** of keys used for historical backups until retention window expires.
- Support KMS key rotation by key alias (AWS): recommend configuring by alias ARN where allowed. Manifest should record the resolved key ARN (and optionally alias) for forensic traceability.

### Failure modes / behavior
- If KMS is unavailable during `backup create`: fail the backup (fail closed). No unencrypted artifacts.
- If KMS is unavailable during `restore apply`: fail restore before any destructive action.
- Error messaging must be explicit (permissions vs throttling vs not-found vs invalid ciphertext).

### Audit + evidence
- Log KMS key ID used, backup ID, and KMS request IDs where available (do not log plaintext keys or wrapped key bytes).
- Emit metrics for encryption step success/failure and duration (ties into ENG-9826).

## Implementation notes
- Use AES-256-GCM with random nonce per artifact. Store nonce in the artifact header or manifest (nonce is not secret).
- Ensure streaming encryption to avoid loading full backup tarball into memory.
- AAD should include: `backup_id`, `cluster_uid`, `format_version`.
- KMS encryption context (AWS) should mirror AAD values to get KMS-side binding as well.

## Acceptance criteria
- `backup create` produces an artifact that cannot be decrypted without KMS access.
- `restore apply` decrypts using KMS and proceeds only after integrity check passes.
- Manifest includes KMS key identifier + wrapped DEK + scheme/version.
- AWS KMS provider works end-to-end in a VPC test environment with least-privilege IAM.
- Docs updated:
  - Installer config reference for enabling KMS
  - Runbook note on key rotation + retention obligations
  - Troubleshooting section for common KMS errors (AccessDenied, InvalidCiphertext, NotFound, Throttling)
- Security review sign-off from Marcus Lin for the provider interface and logging behavior.

## Open questions
1) On-prem HSM: do we target “PKCS#11 via local wrapper” in GA, or document as an extension point for PS engagements?
2) Should we require alias-only configuration, or allow raw key ARN/ID? Current leaning: allow both; store resolved ARN.
3) How strict should we be about restore-to-different-cluster? If we bind AAD to cluster UID, cross-cluster restores will fail unless we support an override. Proposed: default bind to backup_id + format_version only; include optional `cluster_uid` binding gated by a flag. (Need decision in ADR-027.)

## Work breakdown
- [x] Add KMS provider interface (encrypt/decrypt DEK) and wire into artifact encryption path
- [x] AWS KMS provider implementation (using encryption context)
- [ ] Add dev/test provider (local key for CI only) + ensure it is not allowed in production mode
- [ ] Update manifest schema + compatibility checks
- [ ] Add structured error codes and redacted logs
- [ ] Update docs/runbooks (link ADR + operator guidance)
- [ ] Add integration test coverage in staging (requires AWS account + IAM policy from ENG-9825)

## Updates / comments (chronological)
2025-02-05 (Hanae Suzuki): Drafted provider interface. Plan is per-backup DEK + AES-GCM streaming encrypt; KMS only wraps DEK. Confirmed with Marcus that we must never persist plaintext key material.

2025-02-07 (Marcus Lin): Security notes: fail closed if KMS is unavailable; ensure logs do not include ciphertext blobs; include KMS key ID + backup ID for auditability. Also recommend recording KMS encryption context fields in the manifest for reproducibility.

2025-02-10 (Benji Okafor): Wired provider calls into `backup create` path behind `--encryption-provider` flag; added manifest fields (format_version + scheme placeholder). Need compatibility check wiring in restore.

2025-02-13 (Sean Gallagher): Please ensure restore errors are actionable. On-call needs a clear distinction between: permissions, throttling, not-found, invalid ciphertext. Also want a metric for `kms_decrypt_failures_total`.

2025-02-18 (Ethan Park): PR-505 ready for review. Remaining items: docs updates + integration test in staging once ENG-9825 IAM module is merged. Keeping ticket In Review pending security sign-off and end-to-end validation.
